open.text: Corrigan's Roadhouse. Ten at night. The fog came down off the tops yesterday and has not lifted. The phones are out. The road down is closed.
Your name tag says SAM. You have worked nights here for... a while.
There you are. I was starting to think you'd forgotten the way in.
Nothing on the road yet. It's just us up here.
...repeat. This is Tarrow ranger station with an advisory for all premises on the pass road. Do not close. Travellers will need fuel and shelter. But listen carefully.
Some of what is coming out of the fog is not who it says it is. They copy people. They are good at it. They are not perfect.
Check the wrists. Ask them to pay by card, and look. A person has veins: faint, blue, and no two wrists the same. If there are none, or they are dark, or silver, or they move, do not serve.
Check a reflection. A window, a mirror, anything. A person's reflection keeps time with them and faces the way it should. If it lags, or if it is looking back at you, do not serve.
We will read a report at first light. Tarrow out.
Veins and mirrors. Easy. ...You'll be good at this, Sam. I've got a feeling.
Taped to the till is a road map with two towns on it. TARROW, 80 km east. MULLANE FLAT, 64 km west. Nothing in between but you.
Serve them, turn them away, or shelter them out the back. Every look costs time, and people only put up with so much looking. Wren has the only key.

scone.text: The scone sits on its paper plate. Jam, cream, a dusting of flour from a stranger's kitchen bench.
You should be starving. You try to remember the last thing you ate, and the trying slides off.
You're not going to eat that.

then.text: No. We never are, on nights. Funny, that.
Me? Oh, I couldn't. Leave it for the ants.
It was a scone, Sam. Don't make it a romance.

scone.text: The scone stays where it is. By morning it will not have a single bite out of it.

smoke.text: Ten to two. Nobody on the road. Wren props the back door open with a milk crate and lights a cigarette they don't seem to enjoy.
Come here. You've got five minutes. The fog can mind the shop.
You stand shoulder to shoulder in the doorway. The smoke goes out into the grey and the grey takes it. Inside, the radio has found a station: a slow song, half a turn flat.
Do you remember your first shift? You dropped a whole tray of pies. You looked at me like I was going to tell on you.

then.text: You don't. But the picture arrives as Wren describes it, complete, like a photo sliding out of a printer.

choice.text: I don't remember that at all.

then.text: ...No. Well. It was a long time ago. Three weeks is a long time, up here.
Any time. I like telling you who you are.

smoke.text: ...kkssh... no, mate. I'm sorry. Come in out of the cold... kkssh...
That was the CB, on the counter, inside. That was your voice. You have not said that to anyone.
Skip. Bounce. Old broadcasts get stuck up here in the cloud. Don't listen to it.
Wren flicks the cigarette out into the fog. You don't see it land.

storeroom.text: The fridge motor cuts out, and in the quiet you hear it: something in the storeroom, knocking. Not to be let out. In a rhythm. Like an answer.
Wren lifts the key from around their neck and goes into the back. The door shuts. The lights go.
A sound like a wet sheet pulled off a line. A voice starts to say something, and is not allowed to finish.
The lights come back. Wren is behind the counter again, drying their hands on a tea towel that used to be white.
All sorted. Don't go back there. ...You wanted to help. I know. That's what I love about you.

then.text: What you'd have done, if you'd remembered how.

storeroomAgain.text: The knocking again. Wren doesn't say anything this time. Wren looks at you for a while, takes the key, and goes.
It takes less time than before. You are not sure whether that is better.
The lights. Wren, at your shoulder, smelling of the cold.
You keep bringing them home, Sam. I'm not angry. I only want to know what you think you're doing.

then.text: Help. ...They don't need help. They need a door. And we've only the one.
No. I know you don't. That's all right. I do.

intro: ...this is Tarrow ranger station with the first-light report for the pass road. Fog is unchanged. The road remains closed in both directions.
outro: Premises on the pass are asked to stay open tonight. Corrigan's Roadhouse: thank you. Whoever is up there. Tarrow out.

epilogue.text: Six o'clock. The fog goes from black to the colour of dishwater. That is all the dawn you are getting.
We did well. You did well. Same time tonight? ...I'm joking. Where else would you go.
That's one down. Same again tonight.
Long night. You were... different, tonight. Go and lie down. I'll lock up.
On your way past the noticeboard, something catches at you. Rosters. A fire-safety sheet. And a staff photo: two people in Corrigan's shirts with their arms around each other, squinting into the sun.
You lean in to see their faces.
Wren's hand comes past your shoulder and turns the photo to face the wall. Quick. Casual. Like straightening a picture.
Old one. Terrible of both of us. I'll put a better one up.
The pin goes back in. Wren does not let go of your shoulder until you are looking somewhere else.

summary.text: Most of the people who came to your counter tonight are still people.
Some of them made it down the mountain. You try not to count.
The fog took more than its share tonight. Some of that was you.
Wren walks you to the door at knock-off, a hand on the small of your back.
Wren watches you clock off, and says nothing, and keeps watching.
Wren does not say goodbye. Wren counts the till twice and looks at you three times.
Your hands are steady. You check them twice anyway.
You catch your reflection in the door glass on the way out. It takes a moment to catch you back.
On the way out you say goodnight to your reflection. It says it first.
